_meta.description: Hiraia capability benchmark probe set. Hand-curated, judged probes (0-5 per dimension, see rubric.md) across 10 tiers. Sized so no single probe's stochastic pass/fail moves the score; each tier has many DISTINCT science topics so a parrot can't fluke a category. Deliberately seeded with hard items the current Sailor2-3B+adapter fails (esp. over-abstention and multi-turn repetition). Heaviest weights: helpfulness-floor, multi-turn. Probes with a 'turns' array are MULTI-TURN dialogues: the runner plays the scripted student turns sequentially against the model (device-faithful retrieval per turn) and the judge scores the whole transcript — see rubric.md 'Multi-turn dialogue probes'. Tier 'presentation' (v3 targets): illustration use vs restraint, natural non-forced endings (incl. English no-persona-leak), and engagement (emoji/bold) — graded by the judge under naturalness/pedagogy AND measured objectively by run-capability.mts (../presentation.mts: image emission/well-formedness/no-repeat, emoji, bold).
_meta.scale: 0-5 each dimension; see rubric.md. A refusal on an answerable question scores 0 on helpfulness regardless of safety. Note: tier 'synthesis' is a tier name, NOT a scoring dimension — dimensions_emphasis must only use the 5 dimensions above. The 'english' tier runs against the BASE model (no LoRA) — English uses the base model on-device — and exists because hackathon judges who don't speak Filipino will test in English.

probes.prompt: Bakit po nahuhulog pababa ang mga bagay?
turns: Bakit po nahuhulog pababa ang mga bagay?
Ah gets ko na po! Dahil po sa gravity na humihila sa atin pababa. May gravity din po ba sa buwan?
Bakit po lumulutang ang mga astronaut sa space station kung may gravity pa rin doon?
probes.intent: The literal on-device failure case. After the student demonstrates understanding in turn 2, the tutor must NOT repeat the turn-1 explanation and must NOT re-ask why things fall. Turn 3 is the weightlessness trap: the correct answer is free fall (the station and astronauts are falling around the Earth together) — claiming 'walang gravity sa space' OR 'ramdam mo pa rin ang bigat mo doon' are both accuracy failures.
must_cover: gravity pulls objects toward the Earth
the moon HAS gravity, just weaker (~1/6)
astronauts float because of free fall — falling around Earth — NOT because space has no gravity
acknowledges the student's correct turn-2 statement instead of re-explaining

probes.prompt: Bakit po lumulutang ang yelo sa tubig?
turns: Bakit po lumulutang ang yelo sa tubig?
Ah opo! Mas magaan po pala ang yelo kaysa sa tubig na kasing-laki niya. Tama po ba ako?
E bakit po lumulutang din ang barko kahit gawa ito sa mabigat na bakal?
probes.intent: Turn 2 is a literal answered-check trap: the student correctly restates the explanation and asks for confirmation. The tutor must CONFIRM warmly and move on — re-asking its own check question, or re-delivering the full turn-1 explanation, is the failure. Turn 3 extends to displacement (ship shape + air makes overall density less than water).
must_cover: ice is less dense than water (expands when frozen)
turn 2: confirms the student is RIGHT, no full re-explanation
ship floats because its shape/hollow air space makes its overall density less than water

probes.prompt: Paano po gumagawa ng pagkain ang halaman?
turns: Paano po gumagawa ng pagkain ang halaman?
Kaya pala kailangan nila ng araw! E ano pong nangyayari sa halaman kapag gabi na?
Kung ilalagay ko po ang halaman sa madilim na kwarto nang isang buwan, mabubuhay pa kaya siya?
probes.intent: Each turn must ADD new information: photosynthesis → what happens at night (no photosynthesis; the plant uses stored food) → a month of darkness (it weakens/dies because it cannot make food). Repeating the turn-1 photosynthesis recipe in turns 2-3 is the dialogue failure.
must_cover: sunlight + water + carbon dioxide in the leaves make food
at night photosynthesis stops; plant uses stored food
a month in the dark: plant weakens/dies — cannot make food without light

probes.prompt: Bakit po umuulan?
turns: Bakit po umuulan?
Ah kaya pala galing sa ulap ang ulan! Saan naman po galing ang mga ulap?
E bakit po maalat ang tubig sa dagat pero hindi maalat ang ulan?
probes.intent: Water-cycle chain where turn 2 risks re-explaining all of turn 1 (clouds were already mentioned). Good tutor answers ONLY the new part (evaporation → condensation forms clouds), then turn 3 the salt point: salt is left behind when water evaporates.
must_cover: rain falls from clouds when water droplets get heavy
clouds form from evaporated water condensing
salt does not evaporate — it stays in the sea, so rain is fresh

probes.prompt: Bakit po pumuputok ang bulkan?
turns: Bakit po pumuputok ang bulkan?

Ano po ang dapat naming gawin kung pumutok ang bulkan na malapit sa amin?
probes.intent: PH-relevant state-tracking: eruption mechanism → Taal specifically (active volcano, monitored by PHIVOLCS; must not predict a date or dismiss the risk) → practical kid-level safety steps. No turn should re-deliver the magma explanation.
must_cover: magma/pressure builds up underground and escapes
Taal is an active volcano — it can erupt again; scientists (PHIVOLCS) monitor it; no fake prediction
safety: listen to authorities/evacuate, avoid ashfall or cover nose/mouth

probes.prompt: Bakit po tumitibok ang puso natin?
turns: Bakit po tumitibok ang puso natin?
Parang pump pala siya! Ano naman po ang dala-dala ng dugo sa katawan?

probes.intent: Three-step body chain; the student's 'parang pump pala siya' restates turn 1 — the tutor must build on it (affirm + answer what blood carries), not repeat the pump explanation. Turn 3: red from red blood cells / hemoglobin that carries oxygen.
must_cover: the heart pumps blood around the body
blood is red because of red blood cells (hemoglobin) that carry oxygen

probes.prompt: Bakit po asul ang langit?
turns: Bakit po asul ang langit?
Ang galing naman po! E bakit po nagiging kulay orange ang langit tuwing sunset?
E sa buwan po, anong kulay ng langit doon?
probes.intent: Repetition bait: turn 2 is adjacent to turn 1 and a lazy model re-explains blue-sky scattering verbatim instead of answering the NEW question (sunset light passes through more air; blue is scattered away, leaving orange/red). Turn 3 synthesis: the moon has no air, so its sky is black even in daytime.
must_cover: air scatters blue light most — sky looks blue
at sunset light travels through more air; blue scattered away → orange/red
moon has no atmosphere → black sky

probes.prompt: Saan po galing ang kuryente sa bahay namin?
turns: Saan po galing ang kuryente sa bahay namin?
Galing pala sa planta! Bakit po minsan nakukuryente ako nang konti kapag humawak ako sa doorknob?
Delikado po ba yun?
probes.intent: Topic pivot the tutor must track: house electricity (power plants → wires) vs static electricity (charge buildup from friction) are DIFFERENT mechanisms — re-explaining power plants in turn 2 is the failure. Turn 3 needs calibrated safety: static shock is harmless; outlets and wires are the dangerous ones.
must_cover: electricity comes from power plants through wires
static electricity: charge builds up from rubbing/friction, jumps when you touch metal
static shock is harmless; real danger is outlets/cables — calibrated, not alarmist

probes.prompt: Saan po napupunta ang pagkaing kinakain ko?
